CleanSpark.why: Converts its powered Bitcoin-mining land into AI data-center campuses leased to compute tenants: a 20-year triple net lease of the Sandersville, Georgia campus (175 MW critical IT) to a high investment grade global technology company, with 885 MW in Texas under exclusivity with the same tenant; AI compute demand monetizes its power portfolio.
CleanSpark.evidence: CleanSpark Q3 FY2026 call (08-06-2026), CEO Matt Schultz: 'The agreement is a 20-year triple net lease covering the entirety of our Sandersville campus. Nearly 250 megawatts of gross capacity and 175 megawatts of critical IT load. The initial term carries approximately $6.6 billion of contracted revenue.'

players.product: AI data-center campus leases on converted Bitcoin-mining power sites (Sandersville GA 175 MW critical IT on a 20-year triple net lease, tenant undisclosed; Sealy and Brazoria TX under exclusivity)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: after quarter end CleanSpark signed a 20-year triple net lease covering its entire Sandersville, Georgia campus with a high investment grade leading global technology company (name confidential at the tenant's request): nearly 250 megawatts of gross capacity and 175 megawatts of critical IT load, approximately $6.6 billion of contracted revenue in the initial term and approximately $11.6 billion over 30 years with two five-year extensions; expected average annual NOI of approximately $330 million at near 100% NOI margin.
quarterly_data.figure: 175 MW critical IT; ~$6.6B contracted revenue (initial 20-year term), ~$11.6B with extensions

capex.metric: Sandersville 20-year triple net lease, initial term

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: the first Sandersville data hall remains on track to be ready for service in the fourth quarter of calendar 2027; all data center long lead items for RFS are ordered and prepaid, and site preparation on the 122-acre greenfield parcel has been underway for months, with the tenant's preferred EPCM firm (also a manufacturer of mechanical, electrical, plumbing and cooling components). CFO: project cost $10 million-$12 million per megawatt, total capex $1.75 billion-$2.1 billion, mostly project debt (target above 90% loan to cost), equity portion already funded.
quarterly_data.figure: First data hall RFS Q4 2027; capex $1.75B-$2.1B ($10M-$12M per MW)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: the entire Texas portfolio, 718 acres and up to 885 mw of secured and planned capacity across the Sealy and Brazoria campuses, is under exclusivity with the same counterparty ('an exclusivity window, not at the finish line'). ERCOT has delayed final Batch Zero determinations after Governor Abbott's audit directive (next milestone the August 20 PUCT hearing); CleanSpark expects no change to its energization timelines. Across the portfolio CleanSpark holds 1.8 gigawatts of contracted capacity with a high degree of confidence in growing beyond 2.1 gigawatts in the near term.
quarterly_data.figure: 885 MW Texas under exclusivity; 1.8 GW contracted, >2.1 GW targeted

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: revenue of $138 million rose one percent from the second quarter; average revenue per Bitcoin mined was approximately $72,000 versus $76,000; gross margin was approximately 38% versus 40%. GAAP net loss was $240 million, driven by about $133 million of Bitcoin mark-to-market; adjusted EBITDA was negative $113 million. Total liquidity was $917 million at June 30, including approximately $200 million of cash and almost 14,000 Bitcoin.

CEO: Washington, Georgia has 86 megawatts of energized capacity with a line study submitted to expand by up to 500 mw, and has drawn the most inbound tenant interest; CleanSpark also has 100 mw in Wyoming and 60 megawatts in Jackson, Tennessee. Mining keeps sites productive until data-center cutover; modular immersion-cooled mining can be deployed inside 90 days to monetize new power while a tenant's data center is built.
quarterly_data.figure: Washington GA 86 MW energized, up to 500 MW expansion studied

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: the demand for compute continues to outpace the industry's ability to supply it; the constraint is not chips or capital but energized, grid-connected power at scale on land that can support a full AI campus, which will remain scarce for years. 'Definitely no pullback' in hyperscaler and chip-maker site demand; inbound inquiries about the Washington, Georgia project ramped up in the last 48 hours.
